hx_distance_pr — 2D halcon_ext op

• Data kinds: region → feature

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "hx_distance_pr", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

• HALCON equivalent: distance_pr (the HALCON reference is a useful guide to its meaning and parameters)

Usage

The minimum distance from the query point (normalised a, b) to the region (a feature), via the distance transform.

Applies a Euclidean distance transform (distance_transform_edt) to the complement of the region v > 0.5 and returns the value at the pixel given by normalised coordinates (a, b) (the distance from that pixel to the nearest region pixel), divided by max(H, W) and capped at 1, as np.float64.

• a → row min(int(a*H), H-1).

• b → column min(int(b*W), W-1).

• 1.0 if the region is empty (meaning "maximum distance"; note this is the opposite of empty = 0 in hx_distance_pc).

0 if the query point is inside the region. The distance transform is computed over the whole image, so it is heavy for a query of 1 point, but the value is the exact pixel distance (not a vertex approximation as in hx_distance_pc). If you only need containment, use hx_test_region_point.
